transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I came in because, well, I just keep losing chunks of time lately. I find myself constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening the same folders on my computer at work. And before I even leave the house or start my day, I'll sit there mentally replaying conversations I've had. It's like... I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. It's just getting really frustrating to deal with, and it's eating up a lot of my day.
What do you fear might happen if you tried not to re-read the messages or mentally replay the conversations?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't know that I have a specific disaster in mind. It's not like I think... I don't know, that I'll get fired immediately or something like that. I haven't really thought about a specific consequence. 

It's more just this intense, nagging feeling that I missed an error, and if I don't go back and check or replay it in my head, I just won't be able to settle down. The uncertainty just sort of builds up until I have to look again.
When you notice a chunk of time is missing, do you later realize you were carrying out the checking or mental replay, or can you remember nothing about what happened during that period?

Oh, no, I remember exactly what I was doing. When I say I lose chunks of time, I just mean... I get so caught up in the checking or the mental replay that I don't realize how much time has actually passed. 

I don't black out or forget anything. It's more like I'll finally snap out of it, look at the clock, and realize forty-five minutes just went by while I was staring at the same email draft or going over a conversation in my head. So, yeah, I know I was doing it, I just lose track of the clock completely.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different areas of your life, or is this mainly limited to doubts about mistakes in your messages, work, or conversations?

Well, it's definitely not just limited to my work. It bleeds into a lot of different areas. Like, even when I’m right in the middle of trying to work through a system design, or... or preparing a lesson, this thought just keeps barging in. I'll suddenly worry that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled some family photos, or that I let someone in the community down. 

It's really intrusive. And I just can’t seem to let it pass, even though I know perfectly well that I’ve been over it already. So, yeah, it definitely jumps around to different parts of my life.
When you try to resist rereading or mentally replaying things, do you feel driven to do it to relieve the distress or uncertainty, even though you recognize it may be excessive?

Yeah, exactly. That's... that's actually the main reason I finally came in to see someone. I feel completely driven to do it. 

Like I was saying earlier about losing those chunks of time, I'll just get stuck re-reading emails and texts, or constantly reopening folders on my computer to check them again. Or I'll be mentally replaying conversations right before I leave the house or before I can even start my work for the day. I know perfectly well that it's excessive, but I just can't seem to stop. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake, and giving in and doing all that checking is the only way to relieve that awful feeling of uncertainty.
How long have these intrusive doubts and checking or mental replay behaviors been happening this way?

Well, I'm not entirely sure when it started getting this bad. It feels like it's been building up over time, but... I don't really have an exact timeline for you. I just know it's been a problem for a while now.
Have these intrusive doubts and checking or mental replay behaviors been present for six months or longer?

I honestly couldn't tell you if it's been exactly six months. It... it might be. Or it could be longer, or maybe a little less. I just haven't been keeping track of the calendar, to be honest. Like I said, it just sort of crept up on me over time, so I don't have a firm timeframe for you.
Do these thoughts feel like unwanted, intrusive doubts that you recognize as excessive, or are they mainly ongoing worries about realistic problems in your life?

They definitely feel like unwanted, intrusive doubts. I know they're excessive. It's not like I'm just worrying about paying the bills or normal everyday stuff. 

Even when I'm trying to work through a system design for my job, or... or getting a lesson ready, this thought just keeps barging in. I'll suddenly get this intense doubt that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I mishandled some old family photos, or somehow let someone in the community down. And I just can't seem to let it pass. I know I've already been over it a hundred times, but the thought just forces its way in anyway.
On a typical day, do the checking and mental replay take up more than an hour of your time?

I've never actually timed it, to be honest. It... it mostly happens in pieces throughout the day. I'll get stuck on a thought for a few minutes, try to shake it off, and then try to get back to my work. 

I really couldn't tell you if all those little moments add up to a full hour or not. It might, but... I just haven't kept track of it with a clock like that.
On a typical day, would you estimate that checking and mentally replaying events take up at least one hour in total?

I think we just touched on that, but... yeah, I really couldn't say for sure. Like I mentioned, I haven't actually timed it. It just happens in these little bits and pieces while I'm at my computer or doing things around the house. 

If you add all those five or ten-minute stretches together, I suppose it's possible it reaches an hour? I just don't have a solid estimate for you.
Has this pattern of intrusive doubts and repetitive checking been present on most days for at least six months?

I'm not really sure about the exact timeline, to be honest. It... it feels like it's been happening for a while now, but I haven't been keeping track of the months. So I couldn't tell you for certain if it's been exactly six months or not. I just know it's been going on for some time.

When these concerns arise, are they mainly a continuous stream of realistic worries about everyday problems, or are they sudden intrusive doubts that prompt you to check or mentally replay things to feel certain?

They're definitely more like sudden doubts that just hit me. It's not really a normal stream of everyday worries about bills or things like that. 

Like, even when I’m right in the middle of trying to work through a system design at my computer, or preparing a lesson, this thought just keeps barging in. I'll suddenly get hit with this fear that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I mishandled some family photos, or maybe let someone in the community down. And... I just can’t seem to let it pass. Even though I know I’ve already been over it and checked it, the doubt is just there, and I feel like I have to stop and replay it all just to be sure.
How much do the checking and mental replay interfere with your work, relationships, or daily activities?

Well, it's definitely getting in the way. My work has slowed down enough that... well, I've actually missed a few design milestones lately. And I've had to postpone some mentoring sessions that I usually handle pretty reliably. I just get too distracted by it all. 

It spills over into my other activities, too. I volunteer for a youth coding workshop—something that really matters to me—and recently I showed up late and was just totally unprepared for it because I was stuck in my head. I felt really embarrassed about that, to be honest.

I know they're probably exaggerated. I mean, logically, I know I didn't send a terrible message or ruin anything. But... the doubt just feels so strong. It's like my brain tells me, "What if you did, though?" So I don't believe it's 100% true, but I just can't shake the feeling that I need to be absolutely certain, just in case.
Have these doubts and checking behaviors started or worsened after using any substance or medication, or since developing a medical condition?

No, not at all. I don't really use any substances, and... well, I haven't started any new medications recently either. As far as my physical health goes, I haven't had any new medical issues or changes. It just kind of... started happening on its own, I guess.
